{{nihongo|'''Wanikawa Shrine'''|和爾賀波神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sanuki Province]].

'''Wanikawa Shrine''' (わにかわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Miki, Kagawa|arz|بلده ميكى|ca|Miki (Kagawa)|ceb|Miki Chō|es|Miki (Kagawa)|fa|میکی، کاگاوا|fr|Miki (Kagawa)|id|Miki, Kagawa|it|Miki (Kagawa)|ja|三木町|ko|미키정|ms|Miki, Kagawa|pl|Miki (Kagawa)|ro|Miki, Kagawa|ru|Мики (посёлок)|sv|Miki, Kagawa|tl|Miki, Kagawa|tr|Miki, Kagawa|uk|Мікі (Каґава)|ur|میکی، کاگاوا|zh|三木町|qid=Q1205980}}, {{ill|Kita District, Kagawa|ca|Districte de Kita (Kagawa)|ceb|Kita-gun (distrito sa Hapon, Kagawa-ken)|es|Distrito de Kita (Kagawa)|fr|District de Kita (Kagawa)|id|Distrik Kita, Kagawa|it|Distretto di Kita (Kagawa)|ja|木田郡|ko|기타군 (가가와현)|pl|Powiat Kita (Kagawa)|pt|Distrito de Kita|uk|Повіт Кіта (Каґава)|zh|木田郡|qid=Q1155929}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|Q161454|qid=Q161454}}. It is one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for Wanikawa Shrine, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} of {{ill|Miki district|Q10866143|qid=Q10866143}}, {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}.

In Miki there is also {{ill|Wanikawa Shrine|Q11674320|qid=Q11674320}}, likewise read “wanikawa jinja,” and that shrine is also a candidate for the same Shikinaisha<ref>Other candidate shrines include {{ill|Hakusan Shrine (Q11579589)|Q11579589|qid=Q11579589|lt=Hakusan Shrine}} in Shimotakaoka, Miki, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hikimiya Shrine}} in Inoue, Miki.</ref>.

=== Origin ===
The founding period is unknown. According to shrine tradition, Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto rode a {{ill|Shark|Q7372|qid=Q7372|lt=wani}} upstream and landed here. That river is called Wani River ({{ill|Kabe River|Q11675608|qid=Q11675608}}).

There are records of several {{ill|Sengū|Q2271023|qid=Q2271023}} from the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian}} through the {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|be|Перыяд Мурамаці|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845}}. There are four candidate shrines for the Shikinaisha Wanikawa Shrine, and this is presumed to reflect those many relocations.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it became a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Other ===
*The river Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto ascended on a wani later came to be called Wani River, said to be today’s {{ill|Kabe River|Q11675608|qid=Q11675608}}<ref>The other candidate shrines for Wanikawa Shikinaisha, Wanigawa and Hakusan Shrines, identify Wani River with {{ill|Shinkawa River|Q11502062|qid=Q11502062|lt=Shinkawa}}.</ref>

===Access===
*20 minutes on foot from {{ill|Kumonmyō Station|Q11392051|qid=Q11392051}} on the {{ill|Kotoden Nagao Line|Q5364831|qid=Q5364831}} of {{ill|Takamatsu-Kotohira Electric Railroad|Q566998|qid=Q566998}}.
